title: Priority-linearized batching and fair-queue for embeddings endpoint
creator: Lina Chen
description: Problem summary: The embeddings endpoint is experiencing disproportionate p95/p99 latency spikes and throughput collapse during mixed workloads (many small interactive queries + periodic bulk ingests). Root causes observed in prior incidents: head-of-line blocking inside the batching queue, unbounded single global queue causing long tail re-ordering, and naive autoscale policies that react too slowly to bursty arrival patterns. This ticket designs and implements a priority-linearized batching + fair-queueing system with rate shaping and capacity planning hooks to stabilize latency for low-latency interactive requests while preserving overall throughput for bulk pipelines.
proposed_solution: 1) Add a two-tier queue inside the embeddings front-end: a small, low-latency fast-queue for interactive requests (interactive tag or small payloads) and a bulk-queue for large jobs. 2) Implement linearized batching where the fast-queue is allowed to preempt batch windows up to a small fraction (configurable 'fast_preemption_pct') to avoid head-of-line blocking. 3) Introduce tenant-level rate shaping tokens with burst buckets and slow-backoff penalties for excessive bulk traffic. 4) Autoscaling policy: move from single-window reactive autoscale to hybrid predictive/reactive scaling that uses short-term arrival-rate forecasting (EWMA) + backlog thresholds. 5) Add dynamic batching caps per-GPU using observed kv-cache hit rates and sequence length distribution. 6) Add observability surfaces (per-queue p50/p95/p99, preemption counts, dropped tokens) and alarms tied to SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for interactive embeddings (<= 512 tokens/payload) improves from baseline to <200ms at 95th percentile under mixed synthetic load
end-to-end throughput for bulk ingest remains within 10% of baseline when steady-state capacity is available
no increased error rate or dropped requests in canary (error budget preserved)
autoscaler reacts to 2x sustained QPS spike within target window without >20% capacity overshoot
feature flag exists to disable priority preemption and revert to previous behavior

progress_updates: 2025-02-12 - Triage: Incident review linked; confirmed head-of-line blocking patterns. Assigned to Rafael for design + spike.

2025-02-18 - Spike: Prototype linearized batching in local runtime with simple preemption knobs. Observed 2.1x p95 reduction for small queries in synthetic mixed load (fast:bulk=70:30). Logs: https://grafana.redwood-internal/embeddings/spike-2025-02-18
2025-02-25 - Design review: PM and SRE feedback requested tighter preemption guard and explicit tenant rate tokens. Added dependency on ENG-21911 for tenant token service.

2025-02-28 - Load test: 48h mixed workload soak on staging with predictive scaler enabled. Results: interactive p95 median 170ms, but autoscaler overshot by 35% during the first 2 spike waves. Need to tune EWMA alpha and backoff thresholds.

2025-03-03 - Implementation: PR opened for batching changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567. Waiting on CI perf benchmarks and security scan. Planning canary rollout for 10% of traffic in next cycle.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Preemption could starve bulk workloads and increase overall cost. Mitigation: enforce preemption budget and fairness windows; monitor bulk lag and allow graceful degradation via TTL/backpressure.
Risk: Predictive autoscaler misforecasting leads to underprovisioning. Mitigation: maintain reactive thresholds and additive scaling steps; use conservative alpha until stable.

Risk: Tenant-level rate shaping complexity and corner cases in multi-tenant bursts. Mitigation: start with opt-in for large customers and provide default safe limits; roll out with SRE oncall support.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): Enable feature flag for 10% of traffic (non-critical tenants) and monitor p95, error rate, and cost delta for 72h
Phase 1 (expanded canary): 30% traffic with automated rollback if p95 or error budget breach
Phase 2 (regional rollout): enable in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 with per-region knobs
Phase 3 (global): full rollout with config defaults and public docs
